thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: prod-gpu-capacity-critical — cluster prod-gpu-01. queue depth >2500, autoscaler failing to provision GPU nodes for 12m. potential ASG/launch-template auth errors. @devon (on-call) please ack

devon (on-call): ack. I'm on it. joining bridge in 60s

alex (sre): grabbing cluster-autoscaler logs now, pushing trace to channel

alex (sre): kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler --tail=200
```
E03 10:12:34 autoscaler.go:512] Failed to scale up: error launching instances: LaunchTemplateError: Launch template launchTemplateName=prod-gpu-lt, version=7 missing iamInstanceProfile
caused by: AccessDenied: iam:PassRole
status code: 403, request id: xxxxx
```

mari (platform): that 403 on PassRole suggests the LT change removed the instance profile ARN or the role that calls aws:PassRole lost permission. there was a LT rollout ~10m ago (PR #8542)

sasha (eng-runtime): plus seeing taint mismatch in bootstrap logs — new nodes set taint `gpu=true:NoSchedule` but daemonset expects `nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule`. scheduler dropping pods.

devon (on-call): immediate mitigations we can do right now?

alex (sre): 1) rollback launch template to v6 (which had working instanceProfile) 2) if rollback slow, start a manual nodegroup with the older instance profile 3) open ASG quota bump request in parallel 4) route non-LLM traffic to cpu-only region fallback (low perf, but keeps API up)

jenna (support): support seeing ~30% of requests failing on embeddings and heavy generation endpoints. posted initial status page note. customers pinging Slack. keep me updated with ETA so we can update customers.

mari (platform): initiating LT rollback to v6 now (rolling back to exact commit used in v6). will post when change applied.

incident-bot: AUTO-LOG: devon acknowledged paging at 2024-03-15T10:18:09Z

alex (sre): confirmed: applying LT rollback command
```
aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-id lt-0abcd1234 --default-version 6
```

alex (sre): monitoring ASG activity: `aws autoscaling describe-scaling-activities --auto-scaling-group-name prod-gpu-asg`

sasha (eng-runtime): creating manual fallback nodegroup with instanceProfile `redwood-gpu-profile-v2` (spot g4dn.xlarge) to relieve queue while rollback finishes

devon (on-call): queue length: 2520 -> 1100 after initial batch of tasks rerouted to cpu-fallback. thanks sasha.

mari (platform): LT rollback completed, ASG is now launching with instance profile present. nodes are booting.

alex (sre): nodes joined: `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu` shows +6 new gpu nodes. kubelet reports taints as `nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule` now (taint fix came from LT bootstrap script present in v6).

jenna (support): customer errors dropping to ~5% from 30%. removing urgent banner in support channel, leaving notice for 30m monitoring. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: autoscaler error count cleared after nodes joined.

alex (sre): root cause initial findings: LT v7 removed the iamInstanceProfile field (bad merge in infra PR); ASG attempted to launch using LT v7 but instances didn't get instanceProfile so role calls failed (PassRole 403). secondary symptom: LT v7 included a changed userdata that altered taint key. combination prevented new nodes from accepting GPU pods.

mari (platform): immediate followups: locked LT default-version to v6 until controlled rollout, added CI check to ensure `IamInstanceProfile` present before promoting LT versions, adding an infra preflight to validate taints in userdata.

devon (on-call): handing off incident to mari for postmortem writeup and action items. leaving on-call now. pls escalate if customers regress.

mari (platform): creating incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/7923456789 — will include timeline, diff of LT v6->v7, and action items.

jenna (support): I flagged customers contacted and tracked impacted orgs in the incident doc. will coordinate follow-up comms once postmortem complete.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation validated and queue drained. total duration ~48m. auto-close check scheduled in 1h for regression.
